summary: Igarka Airport (IAA/UOII) is a regional airport located in the remote town of Igarka in Krasnoyarsk Krai, Siberia, situated near the Yenisei River close to the Arctic Circle. The airport serves as a vital transportation link for this isolated northern settlement, where road access is extremely limited and air travel remains the most reliable way in or out during much of the year. It handles regional flights primarily connecting Igarka with Krasnoyarsk and other Siberian hubs, supporting both passenger travel and cargo operations essential to the local community.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of Igarka Airport?
A: Igarka Airport primarily serves as a regional passenger and cargo hub for the remote town of Igarka, providing essential air connectivity to Krasnoyarsk and other Siberian cities since overland access is severely limited.

Q: When is the best time to fly into Igarka Airport?
A: Summer (June through August) offers the most reliable flying conditions, as the subarctic climate brings extreme winter cold, heavy snowfall, and reduced visibility that can cause flight cancellations or delays from October through April.

Q: How busy is Igarka Airport?
A: As a medium-sized regional airport with limited infrastructure, it handles a modest number of flights per day, mostly on turboprop aircraft suited to short, often icy runways.

Q: Are there international flights from Igarka Airport?
A: No, Igarka Airport does not offer international service; all flights are domestic regional routes within Russia.
transport_tips: Getting to and from Igarka Airport typically requires a pre-arranged taxi or a vehicle provided by a local contact, as public transit options are extremely limited in this remote town. Visitors should confirm ground transportation in advance, especially during winter when road conditions can be hazardous. During summer, river transport along the Yenisei is an alternative for reaching nearby settlements, though it does not connect directly to the airport.
local_tip: Pack extra warm clothing in your carry-on even in summer—Igarka is north of the Arctic Circle and temperatures can drop sharply, with the airport terminal offering minimal heating and long waits between flights common during weather-related delays.
